examined_formations.title: CHINA_CHENGDU_TEA_FRANCHISE_WITH_COURT_CLOSED_ENTRY_RIGHTS_AND_RESIDUAL_REFUND_BUT_NO_RECEIVED_REVENUE_LEDGER
observed_actor_state_change_evidence: A Chengdu Qingyang District court-supplied 2026 case reports that Yang signed a one-year brand service contract on 2025-06-06 for RMB120,000 and paid an additional RMB10,000 deposit.
The same operator opened the store on 2025-07-27 and closed it on 2025-11-13 because business was poor.
The court article reports roughly RMB400,000 cumulative operator input including service fee, rent and renovation.
The court ordered the brand company to return RMB84,000 of service fee, the RMB10,000 deposit and more than RMB63,000 of equipment/renovation loss.
objective_endowment_or_underuse_evidence: This packet closes an actual time-bounded brand/service right, physical store entry, aggregate investment and a judicially bounded post-closure residual recovery.
The brand company lacked the statutory two-store-one-year condition and had only recently been established, so the licensed control resource itself was legally and operationally weak.
observed_behavior_or_workaround_evidence: Yang alleged missing promised support and information disclosure and pursued judicial rescission after shutdown.

The court verified purchase facts for materials/equipment/renovation through evidence matching the brand company's material list and allocated responsibility 70% to the franchisor and 30% to the operator.
contradiction_or_partial_flow_evidence: The packet is unusually strong on entry cost, executed contractual rights, shutdown date and realized legal recovery.
It does not publish the store's received customer revenue, period-by-period direct operating costs or owner hours/replacement cost.
The approximately RMB400,000 total input is an aggregate investment number, not a complete operating ledger capable of producing normalized net cashflow.
Court-awarded refunds and damages close part of exit value but do not convert the missing operating P&L into known facts.
economic_signal: Executed service fee RMB120,000 plus RMB10,000 deposit; reported cumulative store input about RMB400,000.
Judicial recovery: RMB84,000 service-fee refund, RMB10,000 deposit refund and more than RMB63,000 equipment/renovation compensation.
exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: The decisive control surfaces were the brand/service contract, store lease and supplier/fit-out relationships rather than an operator-owned reusable distribution rail.
The franchisor's weak qualification undermined rather than strengthened the licensed brand/control asset.
No exclusive transferable customer acquisition asset survived closure.

examined_formations.title: CHINA_CHENGDU_RESTAURANT_FRANCHISE_WITH_ADJUDICATED_IP_GUIDANCE_LIABILITY_AND_330K_SETTLEMENT_BUT_NO_UNIT_ECONOMICS
observed_actor_state_change_evidence: A July 2026 People's Court Daily report states that Li paid RMB39,800 in August 2020 to join a branded restaurant project and operated under the franchisor's signage and fit-out guidance.
The operator was sued twice for trademark infringement after following the franchisor's guidance; after the second final judgment, Li paid more than RMB330,000 under an execution settlement.
Li then sued the franchisor for return of the franchise fee and compensation of the RMB330,000-plus loss; the first-instance court supported the claim and Chengdu Intermediate Court affirmed.
objective_endowment_or_underuse_evidence: The franchise contract provided brand and operating guidance as the licensed control input.
The later judgments show that this control input carried a material hidden legal liability rather than a durable operator-owned advantage.
observed_behavior_or_workaround_evidence: After the first dispute the franchisor redesigned the storefront, wall and lightbox, but the new design still contained infringing marks.
Li repeatedly modified the store under the franchisor's guidance before the second lawsuit, showing recurring dependence on the franchisor for compliance and operating identity.
contradiction_or_partial_flow_evidence: Entry payment, a very large realized legal cash outflow and final allocation of that loss are tightly bound to the same operator/control relationship.
The case does not publish customer receipts, food/input costs, rent, payroll, taxes, owner hours or business resale/closure value.
The RMB330,000-plus payment is an externally verified legal loss, not a substitute for the restaurant's ordinary operating P&L.
Final legal reimbursement improves loss recovery but does not evidence a founder-light, profitable or transferable operating position.
economic_signal: Realized infringement settlement paid by the operator: more than RMB330,000; the franchisor was ultimately held responsible for that loss and the franchise-fee claim was supported.
exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: Brand identity and operating guidance were controlled by the franchisor and proved legally defective.
The operator did not own the relevant trademark/control surface and repeatedly relied on the upstream party to redesign it.
No separate operator-owned customer rail or transferable intangible survived the legal dispute.

examined_formations.title: CHINA_XIANGYANG_RESTAURANT_BEER_SALES_INCENTIVE_CONTRACT_WITH_ARBITRATED_EXIT_CLAWBACK_BUT_NO_CUSTOMER_CASHFLOW_LEDGER
observed_actor_state_change_evidence: A 2026 Xiangyang arbitration report states that Wang's restaurant signed a beer sales contract in June 2023 covering 2023-07-01 through 2025-07-01 with a 2,500-case target.
The supplier provided RMB40,000 of conditional sales incentives: RMB16,000 for signage plus 600 cases of drinks asserted at RMB24,000 value.
The restaurant's revenue remained weak and it closed in October 2024; after 15 months it had purchased only 1,300 cases.
In 2026 arbitration, Wang was ordered to return the RMB16,000 signage reward; the supplier's RMB24,000 drink claim failed for insufficient delivery evidence.
objective_endowment_or_underuse_evidence: The contract created a measurable supplier incentive tied to an actual restaurant sales channel and time-bounded purchase target.
The arbitration closes one exit liability and demonstrates how conditional support can reverse into a cash outflow when the point shuts early.
observed_behavior_or_workaround_evidence: The restaurant accepted branded signage support and a minimum-volume structure to lower or subsidize point costs.
When weak operation led to early closure, the supplier pursued the contractual clawback through arbitration.
contradiction_or_partial_flow_evidence: Contract term, target, actual 1,300-case purchase volume, closure and a RMB16,000 final clawback bind to the same operator and point.
The evidence tracks upstream beer purchases rather than customer receipts; it does not disclose restaurant selling prices, total revenue, food costs, rent, payroll, owner time or resale value.
The supplier could not prove delivery of the claimed 600-case drink incentive, illustrating why uncorroborated promised support cannot be treated as realized economics.
The restaurant itself is labor-intensive and the sales contract does not create an exclusive transferable acquisition/control rail.
economic_signal: Two-year target: 2,500 beer cases; actual 15-month purchases: 1,300 cases before closure.
Conditional support: RMB40,000 asserted; arbitrated realized clawback: RMB16,000.
exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: The supplier controls the upstream brand/incentive terms while the restaurant operator controls only the local point and customer service.
The incentive is conditional on volume and continued operation, not a durable transferable asset.
Equivalent restaurants can negotiate beverage supply arrangements; no exclusive distribution/control surface is evidenced.
